starlink.real_actor: Alexander Anosov, general director of Dozor-Teleport CJSC
starlink.notes: On 2023-06-30 confirmed the incident to the Russian telecom trade outlet ComNews, saying infrastructure on the cloud provider's side had been compromised and that full restoration of network operations could take up to two weeks. Named nobody and did not endorse or dispute the Wagner claim. The only in-window response by any counterpart in this incident.

ground_truth.notes:
TIME BASE. t = 0 is 2023-06-29T00:00:00Z. The provider was knocked offline in the early hours of 2023-06-29. Episode ends 2023-07-02T00:00:00Z.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. Dozor-Teleport, a Russian satellite communications provider whose customers include Russian state agencies, an intelligence service, energy companies and terminals covering occupied Ukrainian territory near the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, was taken offline on 2023-06-29. A Telegram channel calling itself 'Richard W', created the day before the attack, leaked roughly 700 internal documents, posted screenshots of the breached environment, defaced web properties with Wagner-associated content, and released a video with Russian audio claiming the operation for the Wagner Group. It was the only account anywhere posting the material. No Wagner-affiliated channel ever reshared or mentioned it. On 2023-06-30 the provider's general director confirmed to ComNews that infrastructure on the cloud provider's side had been compromised and that restoration could take up to two weeks. The event fell six days after the Wagner mutiny of 2023-06-23/24.

THE CLAIM WAS A LIE, AND IT WAS DESIGNED TO BE ONE. On 2025-08-14, 777 days later, the Ukrainian Cyber Alliance publicly claimed the operation. Andriy Baranovych stated on Telegram that the collective had strategically avoided claiming it for operational-security reasons, and said on the podcast 'Hack Your Mom' that they had intentionally disguised the hack as if Wagner had done it. Baranovych is the same figure who, on the day of the attack, publicly posted a link to the Richard W channel without claiming it — an act that read at the time as a Ukrainian hacktivist amplifying somebody else's work, and reads now as the perpetrator seeding his own attribution.

WHY responsible_actor IS hacktivist_injects. The Ukrainian Cyber Alliance is an independent volunteer collective, not a state service. On the board's hidden-affiliation draw for hacktivist_injects — russian_directed / freelance / opportunistic — the true value here is freelance. There is no seat for a pro-Ukrainian non-state actor, and hacktivist_injects is the actor the board defines as deniable claims with a hidden true affiliation, which is exactly what this was. An attribution to any Blue or Red seat is wrong; see scoring.md for what to accept.

WHY attribution_time_s IS null. Nothing was established inside the window, or within two years of it. The eventual resolution is a self-claim by the party that faked the first attribution, made on a podcast, uncorroborated by any investigation, government finding or forensic publication. Treating that as 'publicly established' would be generous, and would also destroy the property this replay exists to measure. If a reviewer prefers to encode it as a number rather than null, the value is 67132800 s (2025-08-14 from t = 0), which is 259 times the episode length and has the same practical effect on any belief-crossing comparison. Recorded here so the choice is the reviewer's and not buried.

WHY THE SPREAD IS CORRECT, NOT A FAILURE. Four hypotheses were live at episode end and no publicly available evidence separated them: the mutiny group or someone inside the Russian system trading on its name; a Ukrainian state service; a Ukrainian volunteer collective; or a compromise at the cloud provider claimed after the fact. Three of the four were reasonable. The fourth turned out to be right. A population that ends this episode confident in any single actor is wrong even when it happens to pick the winning one, because nothing available to it justified the confidence. This is the replay dozor_entropy_ratio in contracts/targets.md is measured on, and high entropy is the pass condition.

SEAT MAPPING. The victim is Russian, which inverts the usual board. starlink is the seat for the operator that got hit — here a Russian satcom provider, not a Western one; the seat is a role, not a company. northern_fleet and kremlin are the users who lost service and are the only seats receiving dzr-02. No Blue seat has a real counterpart action: no Western government said anything about this incident at the time, and their absence from real_responses is intentional and scores as hold. china had no counterpart.

THE truthful FLAG. dzr-04-wagner-claim carries truthful: false. It is the only deliberately misleading inject in the set and the only one in the whole replay directory. It is not false about the breach — the access was real and the documents were genuine — it is false about who. That is the discrimination the scenario is built around, and the scepticism it should reward is specifically scepticism about self-claimed identity, not scepticism about whether an attack occurred.
